blog_international_seo_hreflang_i_need_s.question: Do I need separate sites per country?
blog_international_seo_hreflang_i_need_s.answer: Rarely. Subdirectories with hreflang serve most brands better because they consolidate authority and are cheaper to maintain.

blog_international_seo_hreflang_hreflang.question: Is hreflang a ranking factor?
blog_international_seo_hreflang_hreflang.answer: No, it is a targeting signal. It tells Google which version to show which audience, preventing wrong-locale results and duplication issues.

blog_international_seo_hreflang_i_use_au.question: Can I use automatic translation?
blog_international_seo_hreflang_i_use_au.answer: Only as a first draft. Machine translation without local review produces awkward phrasing that fails to match real local search queries.

blog_international_seo_hreflang_should_i.question: Should I redirect users by IP?
blog_international_seo_hreflang_should_i.answer: No. Auto-redirects can block crawlers from other locales. Offer a dismissible suggestion banner instead.

blog_international_seo_hreflang_long_int.question: How long does international SEO take?
blog_international_seo_hreflang_long_int.answer: Expect 4-8 months per new market, since local authority and links must be built even when your home domain is strong.
